description:
Every test in the workspace runs in the default suite. The property holds today but nothing keeps it: the pipeline measures how many tests were held out and reports the number without deciding on it.

## Background

Tests held out of the default run are unobserved by construction. A held-out test keeps the name of a property, so a reader scanning for coverage finds one and stops looking, while nothing runs the body that would fail. The exclusion also outlives its reason: an exclusion added for an unfinished implementation stays after the implementation lands, and the recorded reason keeps describing a state that no longer exists.

The Rust CI pipeline already takes both measurements this needs. The pinned nextest reporter parses a skipped count from the suite summary, and the doctest step sums an ignored count across binaries. Both are folded into the persisted step summary — `4542 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped` and `63 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored` — and both are currently zero. Neither number is compared against anything.

A doctest that cannot compile has fenced alternatives that keep it in the run or state plainly that it is prose, so holding one out is a choice rather than a necessity.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The project invariant registry declares that every test in the workspace runs in the default suite, and the projected invariant list carries the entry.
- [hard] REQ-02: The Rust CI pipeline fails when a test is held out of the default run, whether by an ignore attribute on a test or by an ignored doctest.
- [hard] REQ-03: The failure names how many tests were held out and in which measurement, so a reader can locate them without re-running anything.
- [hard] REQ-04: A pipeline self-test scenario seeds a tree that holds a test out of the default run and observes the pipeline failing that tree, alongside a clean tree it passes.
- [hard] REQ-05: The invariant records the gate that enforces it, and the enforcement-drift report agrees.

## Notes

The measurements the pipeline already takes are the authoritative ones: a count of what the run actually skipped answers the property directly, where a search of the sources for the attribute answers a proxy for it and matches text that is not a test.
title: Every test runs in the default suite
